scope: Online password verification: unconfirmed results no longer abort a target, native channel loss self-heals once, and unconfirmed counts are shown and retried.
root_cause: A status poll started with only milliseconds left in the 30 s candidate budget, then surfaced as native_rpc_status_timeout; authentication_unconfirmed was raised as AuthenticationTimeout and promoted to a whole-target timeout. Channel-level failures also propagated to the task layer.
behavior: When the candidate budget is exhausted, return unconfirmed without issuing another status request; STATUS polls always get at least one second.
Unconfirmed is not a wrong-key verdict: no permanent attempt record is written, the next candidate is tried, and the candidate is retried on a later run.
A channel-level failure restarts the native channel once and retries the same candidate; if restart fails, the current signal switches to the existing compatibility path.
A capability probe timeout or transport error at target start also falls back to the compatibility path instead of ending the batch.
The compatibility fallback applies only to the current signal; the next signal tries the native channel again.
A per-target timeout still skips only that target and the batch continues; SSH loss, user cancellation and configuration-restore failures still stop the batch.
The records dialog shows an unconfirmed column (latest run only) and states that unconfirmed candidates are retried on the next run.
The summary reports unconfirmed targets separately from real timeouts and other failures.

targeted_run.detail: Known baseline failure in AccessPointTable filters; the failing case does not import or invoke the modified verifier, control channel or records store.

dialog_render.checks: Five columns fit without truncation; unconfirmed header and value visible; hint text not clipped.

schema_migration.detail: Opening an existing password_targets table without the unconfirmed column adds it with default 0.

remote_command_scope: No new router command, option or reply field was introduced; the change reuses the existing control probe, native channel and compatibility path.

official_verification.method: Read the official w1.fi hostap source at tags hostap_2_9/2_10/2_11 and the OpenWrt hostapd package Makefile for each supported series; SHA256 was computed on every downloaded file.

openwrt_series.upstream: branch head at fetch time; same STATUS/event commands as 2.11

findings: STATUS always prints wpa_state, while bssid/freq/ssid/id are only printed when wpa_state >= WPA_ASSOCIATED. The code reads id/bssid only on the COMPLETED success path, so the missing fields in DISCONNECTED do not affect it.
id is current_ssid->id, so id==new identifies the selected verification network. The COMPLETED text comes from wpa_supplicant_state_txt.

WRONG_KEY is emitted only through could_be_psk_mismatch when state is WPA_4WAY_HANDSHAKE, new_connection and PSK (not SAE). Other failures produce no early wrong-key verdict and correctly become unconfirmed.
CTRL-EVENT-SSID-TEMP-DISABLED carries id=<network id> ... reason=<text>, matching the exact-id event check.
disable_network and pmksa_flush exist in 2.9/2.10/2.11; wpa_cli help lists pmksa_flush in 2.9, and the existing capability probe still guards builds without it.
No new remote command or reply format was added; the change only reorders existing status polling and reuses close/open plus the compatibility path.
official_verification.result: No contradiction found between the change and official control-interface behavior. One gap was found and fixed: a capability-probe TimeoutError escaped before the per-target handler and could end the whole batch; it now falls back to the compatibility path.

limitations: No live router verification yet; restart-and-retry, compatibility fallback and real DHCP failure timing still need a real device.
Debian 12 desktop verification was not run.
The three known test_password_target_status table label/color baseline failures remain outside this change.
